subject: Social Media
title: The Consent Illusion
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Consent Illusion usable.

hook.text: You clicked 'I Agree' to terms you never read. Nobody reads them. They'd take 76 days per year if you did.

buildup.text: Terms of service average 7,000 words. Privacy policies average 4,000. That's a novel per platform you join.

discovery.text: A study added 'you owe us your firstborn child' to terms. 98% of users agreed. Nobody read a single word.

twist.text: Consent requires understanding. If nobody reads the terms, nobody consents. Legal 'consent' is a legal fiction.

climax.text: Companies hide damaging clauses in unreadable terms. The law calls this 'informed consent.' Inform whom?

punchline.text: You consented to everything. You understood nothing.

quiz.question: How long would it take to read all privacy policies you agree to yearly?
